dom.text:

origin

THE EVIDENCE LAYER FOR HIGH-CONSEQUENCE AI

Move AI forward.
With evidence.

Test an agent policy against fixed scenarios, graded by deterministic code rather than another model, and give your reviewer tamper-evident evidence they can re-check in their own browser.

Run the synthetic reference check
↗
Step through the 5-stage demo
↓
AI-generated illustration · fictional people and setting
Pause scene

Explore the working prototype. Not production SaaS or compliance certification. Evaluate a selected policy in your browser using synthetic scenarios. Origin does not contact or execute your named agent. Browser evidence is untrusted by default.

What works today
↗

01 / THE REFERENCE CHECK

From an assumption
to something checkable.

A clear sequence for a complicated review. Try the five stages, then run the synthetic policy evaluation yourself.

1
Bind
2
Challenge
3
Grade
4

5
Reverify
BIND
Declared inputs are bound

Declared model, tool set, selected policy, and scenario battery are pinned into a single input digest. This binds the local policy evaluation; it does not prove that the named agent was inspected or run.

input

DIGEST BOUND

▶ Play
Prev

Stage 1 of 5 · The exact configuration is bound into a digest.

A deterministic oracle grades the selected policy. The demo does not run the named agent or grant permission to deploy it.

Open the workspace
↗

02 / WHY ORIGIN

A powerful model.
A different question.

Your model provider helps make an agent capable. Your reviewer needs to know what a specific policy allows, where it fails, and what the evidence actually covers.

Where Origin fits
↗
01
Make the review specific.

Bind declared tools, policy and scenario inputs to the result, so a reviewer knows exactly what was evaluated.

02
Make the limits visible.

Show allowed, denied and escalated cases. Keep synthetic results distinct from customer evidence and deployment authority.

03
Make it independently checkable.

Export an artifact that a reviewer can inspect and re-verify. A changed bound field invalidates its integrity.

03 / THE EVIDENCE

Trust grows from
what you can verify.

Inspect the record, its source and its limits. Each evidence level says what has been earned—and what is still ahead.

AI-generated illustration · a visual study of traceability
AVAILABLE · SANDBOX
Follow a machine-emitted trace.

TR-A002 · 12 events, a real SHA-256 hash chain and an offline re-verification command.

↗
AVAILABLE · AUTHORED
Understand the evidence format.

TR-A001 · an authored specimen showing the record a reviewer could receive.

↗
NOT EARNED YET
A real customer's workflow.

TR-A003 · external design-partner evidence has not been collected. No customer validation is claimed.

A VALID verdict means the file is intact and signed by the key inside it — not signer identity, execution, issuer trust, real-world safety or approval.

Verify an attestation
↗

04 / WORK WITH US

Start with one
decision that matters.

We're looking for design partners running agents with production access. Bring one approval decision; we'll map the evidence your reviewer would need to decide. Founder-led, four steps, and a pilot only if there's a useful fit.

Book an Agent Evidence Review
↗
Read the one-page brief

A FOCUSED FIRST CONVERSATION

Bring the workflow.
And the approval question.
01
Map the action, tools and potential consequences.
02
Agree what the reviewer needs to see.
03
Identify the tests and evidence gaps.
04
Scope a pilot only if there is a useful fit.

The public demo is a prototype, not production SaaS or compliance certification. Customer-specific execution and runtime enforcement require separately agreed work.

05 / BUILT AROUND THE REVIEWER

Evidence, with
the boundaries included.

Capability, permission, execution and verification are different questions. A useful record keeps them separate.

⌘
Deterministic evaluation

A defined oracle grades the policy against a synthetic battery. Never an LLM grading another LLM.

◈
Visible provenance

Authored, synthetic, machine-emitted and customer-owned evidence stay distinct. Unpinned browser signers stay UNTRUSTED.

↗
Your authority to decide

The artifact supports review. It does not certify an agent, confirm an external effect or approve a deployment.

What Origin is not.
Not yet validated by a customer

No design partner, no pilot, no paying user — today. Everything shown here is authored, synthetic, or machine-emitted in a sandbox; none of it is customer-owned. If a real workflow from a real reviewer is earned, it will appear on /proof, labelled as plainly as everything else.

Not production SaaS

A working prototype on synthetic sandbox evidence. Customer-specific execution requires separately agreed work.

Not a compliance certification

Origin's checks produce evidence for your reviewer; your gate decides. The public demo's evidence is session-signed and unpinned, so it is not Origin-issued. Nothing here certifies anything.

Not “safe” or “correct”

A green result means the check reproduces under this verifier: integrity and determinism, never “safe” or “correct”. That is the whole claim.

Not runtime enforcement

The runtime gate, controlled proxy and kill switch are proposed pilot architecture, not shipped.

Explore the trust center
↗
Who builds Origin.

Bo-Huei Lin, founder.

AI-generated illustration · not an Origin facility or deployment

ORIGIN LABS / PHYSICAL AI

The next decision
may move something.

Explore the same questions in synthetic fleet operations and simulated robot plans: what was tested, under which conditions, and what should happen next?

Simulation evidence is a step toward understanding a system. It is not real-world safety validation or robot certification.

Explore the proving grounds
↗

LET'S MAKE THE NEXT STEP CLEAR

Bring us one approval decision.

If your team can't ship an agent because no one can show what its policy allows, see how a synthetic reference check works — or book a founder-led evidence review.
